title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two parallel 3x3 diagrams: a geometric one on top and its profinite group-theoretic ('combinatorial') model below. It answers the question on the previous page, 'Aut ext(π_{g,ν}) = 1 ?', by setting up the framework in which that question becomes an anabelian statement about the Teichmüller tower.

TOP DIAGRAM (geometric). Let k be a field, typically a number field, with Γ = Gal(k̄/k).
- M_{g,ν} is the moduli stack of genus-g curves with ν marked points over k, and M̄_{g,ν} denotes its base change to k̄.
- Rows: 1 → π1(M̄_{g,ν}) → π1(M_{g,ν}) → Γ → 1, the usual 'arithmetic vs geometric' fundamental group sequence. The same row is written for ν+1.
- The forgetful map M_{g,ν+1} → M_{g,ν} has fibre X̄_g \ S_ν (a curve minus ν points). This gives the column 1 → π1(X̄_g \ S_ν) → π1(M̄_{g,ν+1}) → π1(M̄_{g,ν}) → 1, the (profinite) Birman sequence.
- The top row π1(X̄_g\S_ν) = π1(X̄_g\S_ν) records that the fibre group is purely geometric. The Γ column is the identity.

BOTTOM DIAGRAM (group-theoretic model). Let π̂_{g,ν} be the profinite surface group of type (g,ν).
- Aut lac(π̂_{g,ν}) means automorphisms preserving the set of 'lacs': the conjugacy classes of the cusp/inertia loops. Autext lac means the corresponding outer automorphisms. The ° indicates the orientation condition: action on the inertia classes by a single χ ∈ Ẑ*.
- The superscript ! very plausibly denotes the fibre product with Γ over Ẑ* via the cyclotomic character, so that the rows end in Γ.
- T̂_{g,ν} := ker(Autext lac°(π̂_{g,ν})^! → Γ) is a 'combinatorial Teichmüller group'.
- Because π̂_{g,ν} is centre-free (2g-2+ν > 0), 1 → π̂ → Aut → Out → 1 is exact. Taking kernels over Γ gives 1 → π̂_{g,ν} → T̂_{g,ν+1} → T̂_{g,ν} → 1.
- This exactly mirrors the geometric column, with T̂_{g,ν+1} modelled on automorphisms rather than outer automorphisms of the fibre group. This is the standard universal-monodromy picture: π1(M_{g,ν+1}) = π1(M_{g,ν}) ×_{Out π̂} Aut π̂.
- The oblique arrows between the diagrams are implicit. The outer Galois/monodromy representation π1(M_{g,ν}) → Autext lac°(π̂_{g,ν})^! is compatible with the two fibrations. The anabelian hope is that it is an isomorphism, which ties in with the question Autext = 1.

LABELS AND SECTIONS.
- The right-hand labels Σ_{ν+1}, Σ_ν almost certainly denote the sets of (conjugacy classes of) sections of the row extensions over Γ.
- Projection gives a map Σ_{ν+1} → Σ_ν whose fibre over a section s is the set of sections of the twisted extension of Γ by π̂_{g,ν}. Concretely, these are the 'sections of the fibre curve' attached to s.
- This is a fibration method reducing a section conjecture for M_{g,ν+1} to that for M_{g,ν} plus the section conjecture for hyperbolic curves.
- The word under the lower row ('trace'? or a similar abbreviation) is unclear.
- Bottom left: a rational point ξ ∈ M'_{g,ν}(k) gives a decomposition subgroup G_ξ ⊂ T'_{g,ν} (arithmetic Teichmüller group), i.e. a section: rational points → sections.
- Bottom: Σ_{g,ν} (geometric sections) next to Σ̂^{ar}_{g,ν} = Σ̄_{g,ν}. This compares the 'arithmetic' sections of the group-theoretic model with a set Σ̄ (closure/completion of the points or geometric sections). It signals a conjectural identification of sections across the two diagrams.

Overall: a sketch of the section conjecture and the Out-rigidity conjecture for the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}, organized along the Teichmüller tower via the forgetful fibrations.
errors: Exactness of the geometric column and the description of π1(M̄_{g,ν}) as a (completed) mapping class group require M_{g,ν} as a stack (orbifold π1) and 2g-2+ν>0; for coarse moduli spaces it fails. Not stated, but surely intended.

If T̂_{g,ν} is defined combinatorially as the kernel inside Autext lac°(π̂)^!, it is not known (and in genus 0 is closely related to GT, Ihara–Nakamura–Matsumoto results) to coincide with the profinite completion of the mapping class group. Identifying top and bottom diagrams is a conjecture (Oda/Grothendieck-type), not a fact. The page does not distinguish this explicitly.
The precise meaning of the decorations °, ! and of the word under the lowest row is not determined by the page; the reading above is a reconstruction.

ideas.what: Geometric/arithmetic fundamental group sequences for M_{g,ν} and M_{g,ν+1} linked by the forgetful fibration with fibre X_g minus ν points
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Birman exact sequence; outer Galois representation of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmüller tower section; letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: Group-theoretic model: Aut/Out of the profinite surface group preserving cusp inertia classes with cyclotomic character, fibred over Γ, with combinatorial Teichmüller groups as kernels and the Aut→Out tower mirroring the fibration
ideas.modern_name: Out^{C}/Out^{FC}-type groups of surface and configuration-space groups; Oda's problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oda, Ihara–Nakamura, Matsumoto; Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry); Minamide–Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Out of profinite surface groups and the Teichmüller tower in spirit

ideas.what: Rational points ξ of M_{g,ν} give decomposition subgroups/sections G_ξ; comparison of sets of sections Σ for M_{g,ν}, M_{g,ν+1} and for the group-theoretic model
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture for moduli stacks M_{g,n}; fibration method for sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, anabelianity of M_{g,ν}); later Stix, Hoshi and others for sections of fibrations
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) states M_{g,ν} should be anabelian

missed.claim: A fibration approach to the section conjecture for the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}: sections for M_{g,ν+1} are fibred over sections for M_{g,ν}, with fibres given by section sets for the fibre curves. It is set up in parallel for the purely group-theoretic model built from Autext lac°(π̂_{g,ν}), with a comparison Σ̂^{ar}_{g,ν} vs Σ̄_{g,ν}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The section conjecture for M_{g,n} (as opposed to curves) and its comparison with sections of the combinatorial Out-groups is little developed. The page shows Grothendieck explicitly planned an inductive treatment along the tower, combining Out-rigidity and section conjectures. This idea is implicit at best in the literature, though not likely novel to experts.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly the standard Teichmüller-tower / outer-Galois framework that Grothendieck announced in the Faltings letter and the Esquisse. The mildly notable detail is the explicit pairing of section sets Σ_ν, Σ_{ν+1} and the arithmetic-vs-combinatorial section comparison, i.e. an inductive section-conjecture programme for M_{g,ν}. It is only sketched.
transcription_corrections: The groups written 'T̂_{g,ν+1}', 'T̂_{g,ν}' are a hatted T (Teichmüller), drawn with a hat/tilde in the image.

The top row should read 1 → π1(X̄_g \ S_ν) → π1(X̄_g − S_ν) → 1, i.e. the identity on the fibre group. Above it and in the first column, diagonal arrows from '1' make the diagram a 3x3 grid with column 1 → π1(X̄_g\S_ν) → π1(M̄_{g,ν+1}) → π1(M̄_{g,ν}) → 1, ending in a row of 1's.
Similarly in the lower diagram, the columns are 1 → π̂_{g,ν} → T̂_{g,ν+1} → T̂_{g,ν} → 1 and π̂_{g,ν} → Autlac°(π̂_{g,ν})^! → Autextlac°(π̂_{g,ν})^! → 1, with Γ = Γ on the right.
The struck-out fragment under π̂_{g,ν} reads roughly '→ π_g(X_g)' (crossed out).
The word under Autextlac°(π̂_{g,ν})^! → Γ is illegible ('trace'? / 'transc...'); the transcription's 'trace[?]' is uncertain.
At bottom, a crossed-out symbol (G/𝔊) precedes Σ̂^{ar}_{g,ν}; the 'ar' superscript sits under the hat.
